reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that traditional player-first models fail to capture synergies within defensive units. By clustering players into tactical roles (e.g., pass-rushing vs run-stopping), we construct a kernel space where each player contributes to a collective archetype. The EPAoP residual then measures how much a given lineup deviates from expected performance—this deviation encodes the surplus value of teamwork. The model avoids overfitting by using k-means to group players with similar traits, ensuring robustness even with sparse data. This allows GSI to compute posterior distributions over player contributions, while GSE leverages these archetypes for adaptive deployment strategies. Failure modes include misclassification of players into incorrect clusters or insufficient diversity in game-state features leading to poor EPAoP estimates.
